newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha higher, LSWR demand picks up.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha higher, LSWR demand picks up.

text.p: Naphtha prices moved higher in afternoon Tokyo trade on Friday, buoyed by gains overnight in crude values, traders said.
However, upward momentum in naphtha was weaker compared with that of crude due to regional oversupplies, they said.
Offers for second-half July open-spec naphtha were heard at $205.00 per tonne, while bidding levels were notionally assessed at around $203.00.
This compares with late Thursday levels of $202.00/203.00.
First-half July was quoted at $201.00/203.00, after trading at $200.50 on Thursday.
Thirteen potential buyers of Saudi Arabia's term naphtha, including nine Japanese companies, are due to start price negotiations with Saudi Aramco next week in Singapore.
Some traders said Aramco is likely to ask for a $17.00 per tonne premium for A-180 naphtha cargoes to be lifted during second-half 1997 at Ras Tanura. The current premium is $6.50.

In low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) trading, Japan's demand for Indonesian cargoes is gradually picking up as prices of domestically produced cargoes are currently higher than imported cargoes, traders said.
